chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

It was mentioned that Barirah, the slave-girl of Aisha, had a husband who was a slave. When she was freed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Choose, if you wish, you may stay with your husband, and if you wish, you may not.'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: Choice/option, the legal right to choose between two states.
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a specific historical figure and slave-girl of Aisha, used here as the primary example.
key_terms.زَوْجٌ عَبْدٌ: A slave husband, indicating the husband retained his slave status.
key_terms.مَوْلاَةَ: Slave-girl or female servant, indicating her status before manumission.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a freed slave-woman to her slave husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Uthman ibn Isa and Sama'a, establishes the legal principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) for a freed slave-woman regarding her marriage to her slave husband. Upon her manumission, the marital bond is not automatic; she is given the option to remain with her husband or to separate from him, as her status changes independently of his. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding how manumission affects existing marital contracts, emphasizing the woman's agency in maintaining or dissolving the union based on her new free status.
